What the official sources say

  • An owner who believes property is valued too high or improperly valued/listed may file a petition with the county assessor on the department-prescribed form. (A.R.S. 42-16051; source)
  • The petition to the assessor must be filed within 60 days after the assessor mailed the notice of valuation (or amended notice); USPS postmark is evidence of filing date. (A.R.S. 42-16051(D); source)
  • The petition must state the owner's opinion of full cash value and substantial information (income, market or cost approach). (A.R.S. 42-16051(B); source)
  • If the assessor denies relief in whole or part, the petitioner has 25 days after the decision is mailed to appeal to the county board of equalization (or state board if no county board) or to superior court. (A.R.S. 42-16056(C); source)
  • An owner may not appear before the county or state board of equalization without first filing the assessor petition, and may not raise issues not included in it. (A.R.S. 42-16056(D); source)
  • Class three (owner-occupied residential) property is assessed at ten percent of full cash value or limited valuation. (A.R.S. 42-15003; source)
  • Arizona sells tax liens (certificates of purchase) rather than deeds at the first stage; the treasurer later forecloses the right to redeem. (A.R.S. 42-18101(A); source)
  • A real property tax lien may be fully redeemed within three years after the tax lien sale, and after three years until a treasurer's deed is delivered. (A.R.S. 42-18152(A); source)

Arizona evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law. Here is what the official sources say.

  • For nonpayment, landlord gives written notice and tenant has five days to pay before the landlord may file a special detainer action. (A.R.S. 33-1368(B); source)

  • A forcible detainer exists when a tenant retains possession after tenancy ends or after written demand; certain unauthorized occupants may be removed after a reasonable request to leave, with writ of restitution issued immediately after judgment. (A.R.S. 12-1173(A)-(B); source)
  • A tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent for the landlord to enter to exhibit the unit to prospective or actual purchasers. (A.R.S. 33-1343(A); source)
  • The landlord must give at least two days' notice of intent to enter (except emergency or impracticable) and enter only at reasonable times. (A.R.S. 33-1343(D); source)
  • Landlord has no other right of access except by court order or as permitted by 33-1369 and 33-1370, or if the tenant abandoned or surrendered the premises. (A.R.S. 33-1343(E); source)
